hints: x OR y = x means y is a bit-subset of x.
x AND y = x means y is a bit-superset of x.
Use subset and superset sum-over-subsets transforms; subtract disjoint values for the third count.
analogy: Each bitmask is a set of bit positions, turning bit operations into subset questions.
example: For values [1,2,3] and x=1, there is 1 subset-mask value, 2 superset-mask values, and 2 values sharing a bit.
algorithm: Create frequency arrays over all B-bit masks. Apply the subset-sum transform to get counts of submasks and the superset-sum transform to get counts of supermasks. For each x print subset[x], superset[x], and n-subset[fullMask XOR x]. Count duplicates through frequencies.
correctness: The first two transformed sums count exactly the masks contained in x and containing x. A mask has zero intersection with x exactly when it is a submask of the B-bit complement, so subtracting those gives the third count.
complexity: For n values and B bits, O(n+B*2^B) time and O(2^B) space.
